consensus_summary: Primary meaning is abundance, prosperity, and rich divine provision or fatness of the land (context-dependent, no settled single symbol). Common alternatives: remnant subsistence diet under judgment (Isa 7), Christ's true humanity, flattery/smooth deceit (Ps 55:21), hospitality; minority: product of agitation/strife (Prov 30:33).
book_summary: Butter is milk churned solid by labor into sound doctrine: the diet teaching to refuse evil and choose good, the remnant's food, and the wash of walking feet; counterfeit is speech smoother than butter with war beneath.
book_core_identification: sound doctrine (labor-worked solid teaching enabling moral discernment)
boundary_disagreement: Book unifies Job prosperity wash, Isa remnant diet, and Prov churning under a single doctrinal core (positive labor product), while consensus keeps them contextually separate (abundance vs. subsistence vs. strife analogy) without doctrinal referent.
material_contradiction: Consensus primary of material abundance/prosperity cannot coexist as core with book's primary of sound doctrine; accepting the latter replaces the former identification of the same term.
rationale: Consensus responses converge on abundance/prosperity as primary (drawn from Job, Deut, Isa abundance readings) with spiritual/doctrinal senses rare or absent; book replaces that core with allegorical sound doctrine via churning labor + Isa 7:15 discernment diet, reclassifying shared cases (remnant food, foot-wash, flattery counterfeit) under the new referent. This is core replacement, not boundary refinement of the same category, even though some extensions overlap and flattery is retained as counterfeit.
strongest_objection: Key texts (Job 29:6; parallel provision lists) depict literal luxury/prosperity, Isa 7:15 describes a child eating butter to grow in knowledge (not butter-as-doctrine), and Prov 30:33 parallels churning to strife rather than positive labor for teaching; the doctrinal equation is an unsupported allegorical leap beyond even rare spiritual-nourishment alternatives.
